  - Any component or sequence executing time-consuming activity calls `phase.raise_objection(this)`. This increments the phase's internal objection count.
  - When the activity completes, the component calls `phase.drop_objection(this)`. This decrements the objection count.
  - As long as the total objection count is greater than zero, the phase remains active.
  - When the objection count reaches zero, UVM starts the phase drain time timer (if configured via `phase.phase_done.set_drain_time(this, 100ns)`). When the drain time expires and no new objections are raised, the phase concludes.
- **Best Practice:** Objections should be raised and dropped primarily at the test or virtual sequence level. Raising and dropping objections inside low-level sequence items or driver loops creates severe simulation performance degradation.

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- **Premature Termination:** If no component raises an objection in `run_phase`, the objection count remains 0, and `run_phase` exits at simulation time 0.
- **Objection Leak:** If a thread crashes or exits without calling `phase.drop_objection()`, simulation time advances indefinitely until hit by a watchdog timeout.

### Follow-ups
- How to trace active objections? Run with command-line plusarg `+UVM_OBJECTION_TRACE`.
- What is drain time used for? To allow the last driven transaction to propagate through the DUT pipeline and reach monitors before the phase terminates.

title: What is the difference between set_config_ and uvm_config_db*?
answer:
The basic `set_config_*` methods are mapped to corresponding `uvm_config_db` as :

```systemverilog
set_config_int(...) => uvm_config_db#(uvm_bitstream_t)::set(cntxt,...)
set_config_string(...) => uvm_config_db#(string)::set(cntxt,...)
set_config_object(...) => uvm_config_db#(uvm_object)::set(cntxt,...)
```
solution:
> Generated by Gemini via agy.

**Key idea:** `set_config_*` is a legacy OVM/UVM 1.0 mechanism restricted to three predefined types on `uvm_component`, whereas `uvm_config_db` is a modern, statically typed, fully parameterized class supporting arbitrary SystemVerilog types anywhere in the testbench.

| Aspect | Legacy `set_config_*` | Modern `uvm_config_db #(T)` |
|---|---|---|
| Supported Types | Fixed to 3 types: `int`, `string`, `uvm_object` | **Fully parameterized:** Any SV type (structs, virtual interfaces, arrays, enums) |
| Caller Context | Method on `uvm_component` (cannot call from sequences/modules) | Static method on parameterized class; callable anywhere |
| API Signature | `set_config_int("inst", "field", val)` | `uvm_config_db#(T)::set(cntxt, "inst", "field", val)` |
| Compile-Time Safety | Weak (integer casts can silently truncate) | Strong compile-time type verification |
| IEEE 1800.2 Status | **Deprecated** | **Standard methodology** |

### Explanation
- **Legacy `set_config_*` Methods:**
  - Inherited from OVM, the methods `set_config_int`, `set_config_string`, and `set_config_object` were member functions of `uvm_component`.
  - Internally, UVM mapped them to `uvm_config_db` calls:
    - `set_config_int(...)` -> `uvm_config_db#(uvm_bitstream_t)::set(...)`
    - `set_config_string(...)` -> `uvm_config_db#(string)::set(...)`
    - `set_config_object(...)` -> `uvm_config_db#(uvm_object)::set(...)`
- **Why `uvm_config_db#(T)` Replaced Them:**
  1. *Type Safety & Flexibility:* `uvm_config_db` can transfer virtual interfaces (`virtual my_if`), user-defined structs, dynamic arrays, and enums directly without cumbersome wrapper objects.
  2. *Context Independence:* Because `uvm_config_db` methods are static (`::set` and `::get`), they can be called from outside components, including top-level modules and sequences.
  3. *Hierarchical Scoping:* Fully integrates hierarchical precedence rules based on component context.

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- **Bitstream Truncation in Legacy Calls:** `set_config_int` passes values as `uvm_bitstream_t` (typically 4096 bits); retrieving them with `get_config_int` into smaller variable types can cause subtle sign-extension or truncation bugs.
- **Type Parameter Mismatches:** In `uvm_config_db#(T)`, `T` must match exactly between `set` and `get`. Setting `uvm_config_db#(int)` and getting `uvm_config_db#(int unsigned)` fails silently.

### Follow-ups
- How to get values in modern UVM? Call `uvm_config_db#(T)::get(this, "", "field_name", val)`.
- Does `auto_config` field automation still work? Yes, `uvm_field_*` macros generate automatic `get()` calls in `super.build_phase()`.

title: What are the different factory override types?
answer:
Factory overrides can be done in four different ways:

- Instance override by type of the component/object

- Instance override by name of the component/object

- Type override by type of the component/object

- Type override by name of the component/object

Note that calling `create()` with a single argument omits the context needed for an instance override for an object. To provide this context, you can either pass this as the second argument to use the current component's path, or supply a third argument to define an explicit absolute path string.

Read more on [UVM Factory Override](https://chipverify.com/uvm/uvm-factory-override).
solution:
> Generated by Gemini via agy.

**Key idea:** UVM factory overrides are categorized into four mechanisms based on scope (global type override vs scoped instance override) and identifier format (compile-time type handle vs string name), with instance overrides taking precedence.

| Override Method | API Signature | Scope | Precedence | Safety |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Type by Type** | `orig_t::type_id::set_type_override(new_t::get_type());` | Global (all instances) | Lower | High (compile-time checked) |
| **Type by Name** | `factory.set_type_override_by_name("orig_t", "new_t");` | Global (all instances) | Lower | Low (vulnerable to string typos) |
| **Instance by Type** | `orig_t::type_id::set_inst_override(new_t::get_type(), "path", this);` | Specific instance path | **Higher** | High (compile-time checked) |
| **Instance by Name** | `factory.set_inst_override_by_name("orig_t", "new_t", "path");` | Specific instance path | **Higher** | Low (vulnerable to string typos) |

### Explanation
- **Scope (Type vs Instance):**
  - *Type Override:* Replaces every instantiation of `orig_type` with `override_type` globally across the entire testbench environment.
  - *Instance Override:* Applies class replacement exclusively to component instances whose hierarchical path matches the specified instance string (e.g., `"uvm_test_top.env.agent_0.driver"`).
- **Identifier (Type Handle vs String Name):**
  - *Type-based (`set_type_override_by_type` / `set_inst_override_by_type`):* Uses lightweight proxy wrapper handles (`my_type::get_type()`). Checked at compile time by SystemVerilog compiler; invalid class names generate immediate compile errors.
  - *Name-based (`set_type_override_by_name` / `set_inst_override_by_name`):* Uses string names registered with the factory. Flexible for external tool control, but string typos will silently fail at runtime.
- **Factory Lookup Order:** When `type_id::create()` executes, the factory checks:
  1. Specific instance override matching full hierarchical path.
  2. Global type override.
  3. Default original requested type.

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- **Overriding Objects vs Components:** Overriding transient objects (like sequence items) using instance overrides requires passing parent component context when calling `create()`; otherwise the object has no hierarchical path and instance overrides will not match.
- **Placement Timing:** All overrides must be registered before the target component executes `type_id::create()`.

### Follow-ups
- How to inspect active overrides? Call `uvm_factory::get().print(1)`.
- Can an override be replaced? Yes, later overrides replace earlier overrides in the registry.

title: Write pseudo code for implementing an AHB-Lite driver
What does a sequence normally contain?
answer:
A sequence has a task called `body()` within which we can write the actual stimulus to test the design for a particular feature.

Read more on [UVM Sequence](https://chipverify.com/uvm/uvm-sequence).
solution:
> Generated by Gemini via agy. **Key idea:** A `uvm_sequence` encapsulates procedural stimulus generation, containing class registration macros, configuration parameters, optional `pre_body`/`post_body` hooks, and a primary `body()` task that executes the item handshake with the sequencer. ```mermaid flowchart TD START["Sequence.start(sqr) invoked"] --> PRE_S["pre_start()"] PRE_S --> PRE_B["pre_body()
(Optional: raise objections)"] PRE_B --> BODY["body() Task
- Instantiate items via create()
- Handshake: start_item() -> randomize() -> finish_item()
- Dispatch child sequences"] BODY --> POST_B["post_body()
(Optional: drop objections)"] POST_B --> POST_S["post_start()"] POST_S --> DONE["Sequence Execution Complete"] ``` ### Code ```systemverilog class my_packet_sequence extends uvm_sequence #(my_packet_item); `uvm_object_utils(my_packet_sequence) // 1. Knobs and configuration fields rand int num_packets; rand bit [31:0] base_addr; constraint c_pkts { num_packets inside {[5:20]}; } function new(string name = "my_packet_sequence"); super.new(name); endfunction // 2. Main stimulus generation task virtual task body(); `uvm_info("SEQ", $sformatf("Starting sequence: sending %0d packets", num_packets), UVM_LOW) for (int i = 0; i < num_packets; i++) begin req = my_packet_item::type_id::create("req"); start_item(req); if (!req.randomize() with { addr inside {[base_addr : base_addr + 'hFF]}; }) `uvm_fatal("RND_FAIL", "Item randomization failed") finish_item(req); end endtask endclass ``` ### Explanation - **1. Class Declaration & Registration:** Extends `uvm_sequence #(REQ, RSP)` and registers with the factory using `` `uvm_object_utils ``. - **2. Knobs & Parameters:** Class variables declared as `rand` with constraints to allow the test to customize sequence behavior dynamically before starting. - **3. Lifecycle Callback Hooks:** - `pre_start()` / `post_start()`: Built-in hooks called before and after execution. - `pre_body()` / `post_body()`: Optional callbacks traditionally used for phase objection management (deprecated in UVM 1.2 in favor of test-level objection management). - **4. The `body()` Task:** The heart of the sequence containing procedural logic: generating items with `start_item`/`finish_item`, coordinating loops, or starting sub-sequences. ### Corner cases & pitfalls - **Objection Handling in `pre_body()`:** If a sequence is started as a child sequence within a parent sequence, `pre_body()` is bypassed by default unless explicitly enabled, leading to mismatched objections. - **Unconstrained Loops:** Writing unbounded `forever` loops inside `body()` without an exit condition hangs the sequence and test. ### Follow-ups - How to retrieve responses in a sequence? Call `get_response(rsp)` after `finish_item(req)`. - Can a sequence run on multiple sequencers? A standard sequence runs on one sequencer; a virtual sequence coordinates items across multiple sequencers.

title: 為什麼用 UVM？UVM 怎麼做到 reuse？
answer: factory、SV 的多型 / 繼承、parameterized class
solution:
**重點：** UVM 是一套標準化的方法論加 class library。它規定了統一的架構（test / env / agent / sequence）、phase、TLM 和 config_db，再加上 **factory**，讓同一份 component 可以從 block 一路重用到 SoC、甚至跨專案重用，而且**不用改原始碼**就能替換行為。

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph BLK["Block-level env"]
    A1["apb_agent (active)"] --> S1["block scoreboard"]
  end
  subgraph SOC["SoC-level env"]
    A2["apb_agent (passive, same class)"]
    E2["block env (reused as-is)"]
    A3["axi_agent #(AXI_W=128)"]
  end
  BLK -->|reuse| SOC
  T["error_test"] -->|factory override| SOC
  CFG["config_db"] -->|vif and is_active| SOC
```

### 為什麼用 UVM
- **標準化**：大家都懂 driver / monitor / sequencer 的分工，VIP、新成員可以直接接上。
- **stimulus 與 testbench 分離**：test 只選 sequence 和 config，env 不用動。
- **內建基礎設施**：phase、objection、reporting、TLM、RAL，不必每個專案重造輪子。

### UVM 怎麼做到 reuse
| 機制 | 做法 | reuse 效果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Factory | `type_id::create()` + `set_type_override` / `set_inst_override` | 不改 env，就能把 driver / item 換成子類（例如 error injection） |
| 繼承 / 多型 | base class 定義 `virtual` method，子類 override；env 只拿 base handle | 新行為只需寫差異部分 |
| Parameterized class | `uvm_driver #(REQ)`、`bus_agent #(type T, int AW)` | 同一份 code 支援不同 transaction / 位寬 |
| config_db + virtual interface | 不 hardcode 路徑；`is_active` 切 active / passive | block agent 在 SoC 改成 passive monitor 重用 |
| TLM analysis port | monitor 只 `write()`，不知道誰在聽 | scoreboard / coverage 可自由增減 |
| Sequence library / virtual sequence | sequence 疊 sequence | stimulus 跨層級重用 |

### Code
```systemverilog
// 只覆寫要改的部分：10% 機率注入 CRC 錯誤
class err_driver extends my_driver;
  `uvm_component_utils(err_driver)
  function new(string name, uvm_component parent);
    super.new(name, parent);
  endfunction
  virtual task drive(my_item t);
    if ($urandom_range(0, 9) == 0) t.crc = ~t.crc;
    super.drive(t);
  endtask
endclass

class err_test extends base_test;
  `uvm_component_utils(err_test)
  function new(string name, uvm_component parent);
    super.new(name, parent);
  endfunction
  function void build_phase(uvm_phase phase);
    // 必須在 env create driver 之前設定
    my_driver::type_id::set_type_override(err_driver::get_type());
    super.build_phase(phase);   // env 照常 create，拿到的是 err_driver
  endfunction
endclass

// Parameterized agent：同一份 code 給不同位寬使用
class bus_agent #(type T = bus_item, int AW = 32) extends uvm_agent;
  `uvm_component_param_utils(bus_agent #(T, AW))
  function new(string name, uvm_component parent);
    super.new(name, parent);
  endfunction
endclass
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- 用 `new()` 而不是 `type_id::create()` 會讓 override 失效。
- override 要在目標物件 create **之前**設定。
- `uvm_component_param_utils` 不會註冊字串名稱，所以不能用 by-name override（`+uvm_set_type_override`）。
- 過度抽象（太多層繼承、太多參數）反而更難重用。

### Follow-ups
- *type override 和 instance override 差在哪？* type override 換掉全部；instance override 只換符合路徑的 instance，而且優先權較高。
- *config_db 和直接用 handle 賦值哪個好？* config_db 解耦、可跨層級；大型 config 建議打包成 config object，只 set 一次。

title: 什麼是 functional coverage？
怎麼驗證 sync FIFO？
answer: 用哪些 UVM component、scoreboard、coverage、testcase、corner case（作者事先準備過這題）
solution:
**重點：** 用 UVM agent 驅動 write / read 兩端，monitor 把每個 cycle 的操作送到用 **SV queue 當 reference model** 的 scoreboard，資料和 `full` / `empty` flag 都要比；再用 coverage 確認 full、empty、wrap-around、同時讀寫都有打到，並用 assertion 守住 overflow / underflow。

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  TEST["test (selects vseq + config)"] --> VSEQ["virtual sequence"]
  VSEQ --> WAGT
  VSEQ --> RAGT
  subgraph ENV["fifo_env"]
    WAGT["write agent: sqr, drv, mon"]
    RAGT["read agent: sqr, drv, mon"]
    SCB["scoreboard: queue model"]
    COV["coverage subscriber"]
  end
  WAGT -->|wr_en, wdata| DUT["sync FIFO DUT"]
  RAGT -->|rd_en| DUT
  DUT -->|rdata and flags| MON["monitor"]
  MON -->|analysis port| SCB
  MON -->|analysis port| COV
  SVA["SVA bound to DUT"] -.-> DUT
```

### Scoreboard（核心）
```systemverilog
import fifo_pkg::*;   // 提供 W、DEPTH 和 fifo_item

class fifo_scb extends uvm_scoreboard;
  `uvm_component_utils(fifo_scb)
  uvm_analysis_imp #(fifo_item, fifo_scb) imp;
  bit [W-1:0] model_q[$];

  function new(string name, uvm_component parent);
    super.new(name, parent);
    imp = new("imp", this);
  endfunction

  // monitor 每個 cycle 送一筆：wr_en, rd_en, wdata, rdata（已依讀取延遲對齊）, full, empty
  function void write(fifo_item t);
    int n = model_q.size();                   // 操作前的狀態
    if (t.full  !== (n == DEPTH)) `uvm_error("FLAG", $sformatf("full=%0b, model level=%0d", t.full, n))
    if (t.empty !== (n == 0))     `uvm_error("FLAG", $sformatf("empty=%0b, model level=%0d", t.empty, n))
    if (t.rd_en && n > 0) begin               // underflow 讀取要被忽略
      bit [W-1:0] exp = model_q.pop_front();
      if (t.rdata !== exp) `uvm_error("DATA", $sformatf("rdata=%h exp=%h", t.rdata, exp))
    end
    if (t.wr_en && n < DEPTH)                 // 依 spec：full 時寫入被丟棄
      model_q.push_back(t.wdata);
  endfunction

  function void check_phase(uvm_phase phase);
    if (model_q.size() != 0) `uvm_info("SCB", $sformatf("%0d entries left in FIFO", model_q.size()), UVM_LOW)
  endfunction
endclass
```

### Testcases
| Test | 目的 |
| --- | --- |
| fill-to-full 再 drain-to-empty | flag 時序、pointer wrap |
| write when full / read when empty | overflow / underflow 保護 |
| full 時同時讀寫、empty 時同時讀寫 | 依 spec 的 push / pop 優先權 |
| 長時間 random 讀寫（各種讀寫比例） | 資料完整性、wrap 多次 |
| 中途 reset | pointer / flag 回到初始值 |
| 參數化：DEPTH = 1、非 2 的冪次 | pointer 邊界 |

### Coverage 與 assertion
- coverage：level 的 bins（0、1、DEPTH-1、DEPTH）× 操作 {idle, rd, wr, both}；`full` / `empty` 的 0→1、1→0 transition；read / write pointer 的 wrap。
- SVA：`!(full && empty)`；`full && wr_en && !rd_en |=> $stable(level)`；`empty |-> !rd_valid`。

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- 讀取延遲（first-word-fall-through 或 1-cycle registered）要在 monitor 對齊，否則 scoreboard 全部錯位。
- 同時讀寫時，model 必須用**操作前**的 level 判斷能不能讀 / 寫。
- 寫入資料用 all-0 / all-1 / walking-1，才抓得到 bit 短路或接錯。

### Follow-ups
- *async FIFO 要多驗什麼？* gray-code pointer、synchronizer、不同時脈比例，加上 CDC 工具和 metastability injection。
- *怎麼知道驗完了？* vplan 的 coverage 100%、code coverage 的漏洞都有說明、regression 穩定通過。

title: OOP 繼承與多型
answer: 給一段 code，判斷 virtual function override 的行為；寫一個展示多型、向上 / 向下轉型的例子，並說明實際工作中的使用情境
solution:
**重點：** `virtual` function 依**物件實際型別**決定呼叫哪個版本（動態綁定）；non-virtual 依 **handle 的型別**決定（靜態綁定）。子類轉成父類（upcast）一定合法、可以隱式轉換；父類轉成子類（downcast）必須用 `$cast` 在 runtime 檢查。

| 呼叫（`Animal a = new Dog`） | 結果 | 原因 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `a.speak()`（non-virtual） | `Animal::speak` | 看 handle 型別 |
| `a.move()`（virtual） | `Dog::move` | 看物件型別 |
| `a.fetch()` | compile error | `Animal` 沒有 `fetch` |
| `$cast(d2, a)` | 成功（回傳 1） | 物件本來就是 `Dog` |
| `a = new(); $cast(d2, a)` | 失敗（回傳 0） | 物件是純 `Animal` |

### Code
```systemverilog
class Animal;
  function void speak();        $display("Animal::speak"); endfunction  // non-virtual
  virtual function void move(); $display("Animal::move");  endfunction
endclass

class Dog extends Animal;
  function void speak();        $display("Dog::speak");    endfunction  // 只是 hide
  virtual function void move(); $display("Dog::move");     endfunction  // override
  function void fetch();        $display("Dog::fetch");    endfunction
endclass

module top;
  initial begin
    Animal a;
    Dog    d, d2;
    d = new();
    a = d;                 // upcast：隱式、永遠合法
    a.speak();             // Animal::speak
    a.move();              // Dog::move
    d.speak();             // Dog::speak
    if ($cast(d2, a)) d2.fetch();          // downcast 成功 -> Dog::fetch
    a = new();             // 純 Animal 物件
    if (!$cast(d2, a)) $display("downcast failed: object is not a Dog");
  end
endmodule
```

### Explanation
- 父類一旦宣告 `virtual`，子類同名 method 自動是 virtual（可省略關鍵字，但建議寫出來）。
- 子類可以用 `super.move()` 呼叫父類版本，擴充而不是重寫。
- `$cast` 用成 function 時，失敗回傳 0；用成 task（`$cast(d2, a);`）時，失敗會報 runtime error。

### 實際工作中的使用情境
- **Error injection**：`err_driver extends my_driver`，override `virtual drive()`，再用 factory override，env 完全不用改。
- **Sequence item 擴充**：`axi_item` → `axi_err_item` 多加 constraint 或欄位。
- **`do_copy` / `do_compare`**：參數型別是 `uvm_object rhs`，要先 `$cast(rhs_, rhs)` 才能存取子類欄位（典型 downcast）。
- **Callback**：base callback class 定義空的 virtual hook，使用者繼承後實作。

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- 忘了 `virtual` → 透過父類 handle 呼叫時，永遠跑父類版本（最常見的面試陷阱）。
- override 的 virtual method 參數和回傳型別必須一致。
- constructor `new()` 不能是 virtual；constraint 會依名稱被子類同名 constraint 覆蓋。

### Follow-ups
- *pure virtual 是什麼？* `pure virtual function void f();` 只能放在 `virtual class`（abstract），子類必須實作。
- *static method 可以 virtual 嗎？* 不行，static 沒有物件，無從動態綁定。

title: 找出 monitor 程式碼的 bug
answer:
- interrupt 比 write function 早到，所以 write 永遠不會被中斷（邏輯錯誤）
- 沒用 `automatic` 變數 → 不同的 function call 會互相干擾
solution:
**重點：** 這題常見的兩個 bug：(1) monitor 用 **edge 事件** `@(posedge irq)` 等 interrupt，但 interrupt 比 write 檢查開始得早，事件已經過去，所以永遠等不到，「write 被中斷」的路徑永遠不會執行（邏輯錯誤）；(2) task 沒宣告成 `automatic`（module / interface 裡預設是 **static**），同時 fork 出來的多個呼叫共用同一份區域變數，互相覆蓋。

```wavedrom
{ "signal": [
  { "name": "clk",         "wave": "p........" },
  { "name": "irq",         "wave": "01......." },
  { "name": "wr_en",       "wave": "0.10....." },
  { "name": "check_write", "wave": "x..=...x.", "data": ["waiting @(posedge irq): edge already gone"] }
],
  "head": { "text": "irq rose before the task started waiting, so the event is missed" } }
```

### 有 bug 的 monitor（重建的原題寫法）
```systemverilog
module bus_mon (input logic clk, wr_en, irq, input logic [31:0] addr, wdata);
  task check_write(input logic [31:0] a, d);       // BUG 2：module 內的 task 預設 static
    logic [31:0] a_l, d_l;                         //   所有並行呼叫共用 a_l / d_l
    a_l = a; d_l = d;
    fork
      begin @(posedge irq); $display("write %h interrupted", a_l); end  // BUG 1：edge 已過
      repeat (4) @(posedge clk);
    join_any
    disable fork;
    $display("write done addr=%h data=%h", a_l, d_l);   // 可能印出別筆 write 的值
  endtask

  always @(posedge clk) if (wr_en) fork check_write(addr, wdata); join_none
endmodule
```

### 修正版
```systemverilog
module bus_mon (input logic clk, wr_en, irq, input logic [31:0] addr, wdata);
  task automatic check_write(input logic [31:0] a, d);   // 每次呼叫有自己的變數
    bit interrupted = 0;
    fork
      begin wait (irq === 1'b1); interrupted = 1; end    // level-sensitive，不會錯過
      repeat (4) @(posedge clk);
    join_any
    disable fork;
    if (interrupted) $display("%0t: write %h interrupted", $time, a);
    else             $display("%0t: write done addr=%h data=%h", $time, a, d);
  endtask

  always @(posedge clk) if (wr_en) fork check_write(addr, wdata); join_none
endmodule
```

### Explanation
- `@(event)` 只會等**之後**發生的 edge；條件可能早已成立時，要用 `wait(expr)`（level）、記錄時間戳，或把 interrupt 狀態存成 flag，在檢查時讀取。
- class 裡的 method 預設就是 automatic；module / interface / program 裡的 task / function 預設是 static，legacy testbench 最常踩到。
- 同一個 time step 內的 race（irq 和 wr_en 同一個 edge 改變）也要考慮：用 clocking block 或 `#1step` 取樣。

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- `disable fork` 會殺掉呼叫者底下**所有** child process；在共用 process 裡要用 `fork begin ... end join` 把它包起來隔離。
- 「interrupt 在 write 之前就已經 high」到底算不算中斷，要先和 spec 確認；修正版把它當成中斷。

### Follow-ups
- *怎麼避免 static 變數的問題？* 用 `task automatic` / `function automatic`，或在 module 開頭宣告 `module automatic bus_mon`。
- *UVM monitor 會有一樣的問題嗎？* class task 是 automatic，但如果把 transaction 物件重複使用（沒有每次 `create`），也會發生同樣的覆蓋問題。

title: 職涯中遇過最難的 bug
answer: （behavioral，要事先準備故事）
solution:
**重點：** 用 **STAR**（Situation / Task / Action / Result）講一個**你自己真的追過**的 bug，重點放在「怎麼縮小範圍、怎麼證明 root cause、怎麼避免再發生」。技術深度和 debug 方法論比 bug 本身更重要。

| STAR | 範例回答（請換成自己的故事） |
| --- | --- |
| **Situation** | DMA block 的 regression 中，大約每 3000 個 seed 才有 1 個 fail：scoreboard 報 descriptor 的資料錯一個 word，而且只在 SoC level、開啟 clock gating 時出現。 |
| **Task** | 我負責判斷是 TB 還是 RTL 的問題，並在 tape-out freeze 前兩週找到 root cause。 |
| **Action** | 1) 先固定 seed 重現，再寫 script 掃描所有 fail seed 的共同點：都在 AXI back-pressure 期間發生 clock-gate 開關。2) 縮小成 directed test：只保留 back-pressure + 進入 / 離開 gating，fail 率變成 100%。3) 看波形發現 gating 解除那一拍，`wready` 和 enable 的 latch 晚了一拍，FIFO 的 write pointer 多推進一次。4) 加 SVA `!clk_en |-> $stable(wptr)` 立刻抓到，和 designer 確認是 ICG enable 少了一級 flop。 |
| **Result** | RTL 修正後 10 萬個 seed 都 pass；SVA 加進 regression 永久保留；我也在 coverage 加了「back-pressure × clock gating」的 cross，事後發現原本這個 cross 的 coverage 是 0%，於是在 vplan 補上低功耗互動的章節。 |

### 講法重點
- **難在哪裡要講清楚**：低機率、只在特定組合出現、波形很長、跨 clock domain、gate-level 才出現等。
- **方法論**：重現 → 縮小 → 假設 → 用證據（波形、assertion、log）證明 → 修正 → 防止再發生（assertion、coverage、checklist）。
- **量化結果**：fail 率、花了多久、救了多少時程、之後抓到幾個類似 bug。
- **團隊合作**：怎麼和 designer 溝通，例如帶著最小重現 test 和波形去，而不是只說「你的 RTL 壞了」。

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- 不要講太簡單的 bug（例如 typo），也不要講你只是旁觀的 bug。
- 不要怪別人；把重點放在你採取的行動。
- 準備好被追問細節：signal 名稱、為什麼原本的 coverage 沒抓到、你會怎麼改 TB。

### Follow-ups
- *如果無法重現怎麼辦？* 記錄更多資訊（transaction log、assertion）、加大 random 壓力、比對 fail 和 pass seed 的差異。
- *事後學到什麼？* 例如「低功耗與 traffic 的交互作用要在 vplan 明確列出」。

title: Sequence detector FSM
answer: Moore vs Mealy、overlapping vs non-overlapping
solution:
**重點：** **Moore** 的輸出只看目前 state（要多一個「偵測到」的 state，輸出晚一拍但不會 glitch）；**Mealy** 的輸出看 state 加上目前輸入（state 較少、同一拍就輸出，但會把輸入的 glitch 傳到輸出）。**Overlapping** 偵測到後回到「最長後綴等於前綴」的 state；**non-overlapping** 偵測到後回到 idle。以下以偵測 `101` 為例。

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> S0
  S0 --> S1: 1/0
  S0 --> S0: 0/0
  S1 --> S1: 1/0
  S1 --> S2: 0/0
  S2 --> S1: 1/1 (overlap)
  S2 --> S0: 0/0
```
Mealy、overlapping（`S0` = 還沒匹配，`S1` = 看到 `1`，`S2` = 看到 `10`）。non-overlapping 時只把 `S2 --1/1--> S1` 改成 `S2 --1/1--> S0`。

### 比較
| | Moore | Mealy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 輸出取決於 | state | state + input |
| `101` 需要的 state 數 | 4（多一個 `S3`，輸出 1） | 3 |
| 輸出時間 | 最後一個 bit 的**下一拍** | 最後一個 bit 的**同一拍** |
| Glitch | 輸出只來自 flop，乾淨 | 輸入的 glitch 會傳到輸出 |
| Timing | 輸出 path 短 | input → output 是組合邏輯路徑 |

### Overlapping vs non-overlapping（輸入 `10101`）
| bit | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| overlapping 輸出 | 0 | 0 | **1** | 0 | **1** |
| non-overlapping 輸出 | 0 | 0 | **1** | 0 | 0 |

### Code（Mealy、overlapping）
```systemverilog
module det101_mealy (input logic clk, rst_n, din, output logic dout);
  typedef enum logic [1:0] {S0, S1, S2} state_t;
  state_t state, nxt;

  always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)
    if (!rst_n) state <= S0;
    else        state <= nxt;

  always_comb begin
    nxt  = state;
    dout = 1'b0;
    unique case (state)
      S0: nxt = din ? S1 : S0;
      S1: nxt = din ? S1 : S2;
      S2: begin
            nxt  = din ? S1 : S0;   // non-overlapping：din ? S0 : S0
            dout = din;             // 看到 "101"
          end
    endcase
  end
endmodule
```
Moore 版：加 `S3`（輸出 1），`S2 --1--> S3`；`S3 --1--> S1`、`S3 --0--> S2`（overlapping），`dout = (state == S3)`。

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- overlapping 時回到哪個 state 要用「最長的後綴 = 前綴」推，例如 `1101` 偵測完回到「看到 `1`」。
- Mealy 輸出如果要 registered，就等於又變成晚一拍（實質上變成 Moore）。
- reset 後第一個 bit、連續的 `1111`、`0000` 都要測。

### Follow-ups
- *怎麼驗證？* 用 sliding-window reference model（shift register 和 pattern 比較）對大量 random bit 比對；coverage 收每個 state 與每條 transition。
- *one-hot 還是 binary 編碼？* one-hot 的 next-state 邏輯較快、適合 FPGA；binary 用的 flop 較少。

title: Computer architecture
answer:
pipeline stages、pipeline hazards
---
solution:
**重點：** 經典 5-stage pipeline：**IF → ID → EX → MEM → WB**，理想上每個 cycle 完成一道指令（CPI = 1）。pipeline hazard 有三種：**structural**（硬體資源衝突）、**data**（指令之間的資料相依，RAW 最常見）、**control**（branch / jump 還沒決定前就抓了後面的指令）。解法是 forwarding、stall（bubble）、flush 和 branch prediction。

### Pipeline 圖：load-use hazard（一定要 stall 1 cycle）
| 指令 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lw  x1, 0(x2)` | IF | ID | EX | MEM | WB | | | |
| `add x3, x1, x4` | | IF | ID | **stall** | EX | MEM | WB | |
| `sub x5, x3, x6` | | | IF | **stall** | ID | EX | MEM | WB |

- `lw` 的資料在第 4 拍 MEM 結束才有，`add` 的 EX 最早只能在第 5 拍，資料從 MEM/WB 暫存器 **forward** 過去。
- `sub` 需要的 `x3` 在第 6 拍從 EX/MEM forward 過去，不必再 stall。

### Hazard 種類與解法
| Hazard | 例子 | 解法 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Structural | 指令和資料共用一個 memory port | 分開 I-cache / D-cache、增加 port、stall |
| Data RAW | `add x1,..` 接著 `sub ..,x1,..` | forwarding（EX→EX、MEM→EX）；load-use 要 stall 1 拍；compiler 重排指令 |
| Data WAR / WAW | out-of-order 或多個寫回 stage 才會發生 | register renaming（in-order 5-stage 不會有） |
| Control | `beq` 在 EX 才知道要不要跳 | 預測 not-taken + flush、在 ID 提早算 branch、branch prediction（BHT / BTB）、delay slot |

### Explanation
- **pipeline 暫存器**（IF/ID、ID/EX、EX/MEM、MEM/WB）把每個 stage 隔開；stall 的做法是凍結 PC 和 IF/ID，並在 ID/EX 插入 NOP（bubble）。
- **Hazard detection unit**（在 ID）：`ID/EX.MemRead && (ID/EX.rd == IF/ID.rs1 || ID/EX.rd == IF/ID.rs2)` 就 stall。
- **Forwarding unit**（在 EX）：比對 EX/MEM.rd、MEM/WB.rd 和目前指令的 rs1 / rs2（`rd != x0`），EX/MEM 的優先權較高（資料較新）。
- 分支預測錯誤的代價 = 在決定 branch 之前已經抓進來的指令數（branch 在 EX 決定就是 2 拍）。

### 從 DV 的角度怎麼驗
- 和 ISS（instruction set simulator）**lockstep 比對**：每道指令 retire 時比 PC、寫回的 register、memory store。
- coverage：每種 forwarding 路徑、load-use stall、branch taken / not-taken × 預測對 / 錯、連續相依的指令、寫 `x0`。
- random instruction generator 搭配 constraint，刻意產生大量相依的指令。

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- 寫 `x0` 不能被 forward（`x0` 永遠是 0）。
- 同時有 EX/MEM 和 MEM/WB 兩個可 forward 的來源時，要選最新的。
- stall 和 flush 同一拍發生（例如 load-use 之後馬上遇到 mispredict）時的優先權。

### Follow-ups
- *pipeline 越深越好嗎？* 頻率較高，但 hazard 的代價（mispredict penalty）變大，CPI 變差。
- *superscalar / out-of-order 怎麼處理 hazard？* register renaming、reservation station、ROB 依序 retire。

title: Blocking vs non-blocking assignment
solution:
**Key idea:** A blocking assignment (`=`) updates the variable **immediately**, so the next statement sees the new value. A non-blocking assignment (`<=`) samples its right-hand side now and updates the left-hand side **at the end of the time step** (NBA region), so every flop "reads old, writes new" in parallel. Rule of thumb: `<=` in clocked `always_ff`, `=` in combinational `always_comb`.

```wavedrom
{ "signal": [
  { "name": "clk",               "wave": "p......." },
  { "name": "d",                 "wave": "01.0...." },
  { "name": "q1",                "wave": "0.1.0..." },
  { "name": "q2 (non-blocking)", "wave": "0..1.0.." },
  { "name": "q2 (blocking)",     "wave": "0.1.0..." }
],
  "head": { "text": "with blocking, q2 copies the NEW q1: the 2-stage shift register collapses to 1 stage" } }
```

### Code
```systemverilog
// Correct: 2-stage shift register
always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
  q1 <= d;
  q2 <= q1;      // old q1
end

// Wrong: q2 gets the new q1, so both flops hold d
always @(posedge clk) begin
  q1 = d;
  q2 = q1;
end

// Swap: works only with non-blocking
always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
  a <= b;
  b <= a;
end

// Combinational: blocking, evaluated in order
always_comb begin
  sum   = a + b;
  carry = sum[8];   // uses the value computed one line above
end
```

| | Blocking `=` | Non-blocking `<=` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Update time | immediately (Active region) | end of time step (NBA region) |
| Later statements see | new value | old value |
| Use for | combinational logic, temporaries, testbench procedural code | sequential logic (flops), and any variable read by another clocked block |
| Order of statements | matters | does not matter for the result |

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- **Race between always blocks:** two `always @(posedge clk)` blocks using `=` (one writes `x`, the other reads `x`) give simulator-order-dependent results; NBA removes the race.
- Mixing `=` and `<=` on the same variable is illegal in `always_ff` and a bad idea anywhere.
- Using `<=` in combinational logic simulates correctly but can need extra delta cycles, and reading the variable in the same block gives the stale value.
- Synthesis gives the same netlist only if the code follows the guidelines; otherwise simulation and synthesis differ.

### Follow-ups
- *What are the scheduler regions?* Preponed → Active (blocking, RHS of NBAs evaluated) → Inactive (`#0`) → NBA (LHS updates) → Observed (assertions) → Reactive (program / checker code) → Postponed (`$strobe`, `$monitor`).
- *What does `$display` show right after `q <= 1`?* The old value; `$strobe` shows the final value of the time step.

title: 在 log file 裡搜尋關鍵字並取代（腳本）
solution:
**重點：** 小檔案、一次性的就用 `sed -i` 或 `perl -pi -e` 一行解決；需要統計替換次數、條件替換或處理很大的 log 時，寫 Python / Perl script，**逐行串流處理**並輸出到新檔（或先備份），不要整個檔案讀進記憶體。

| 工具 | 指令 | 備註 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| grep | `grep -n "TIMEOUT" sim.log` | 先找出位置和次數（`-c` 只算次數） |
| sed | `sed -i.bak 's/TIMEOUT/TIME_OUT/g' sim.log` | `-i.bak` 原地修改並保留備份 |
| perl | `perl -pi.bak -e 's/\bTIMEOUT\b/TIME_OUT/g' *.log` | regex 功能最完整，可一次處理多個檔案 |
| python | 見下方 | 可計數、可加條件、可移植 |

### Code
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Usage: replace.py <log> <regex> <replacement> [-o out.log]
import argparse
import re
import sys


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("log")
    ap.add_argument("pattern")
    ap.add_argument("repl")
    ap.add_argument("-o", "--out", help="output file (default: <log>.new)")
    args = ap.parse_args()

    rx = re.compile(args.pattern)
    out_path = args.out or args.log + ".new"
    total = lines_hit = 0
    with open(args.log, errors="replace") as fin, open(out_path, "w") as fout:
        for lineno, line in enumerate(fin, 1):
            new, n = rx.subn(args.repl, line)       # subn 回傳 (新字串, 替換次數)
            if n:
                total += n
                lines_hit += 1
                print(f"{lineno}: {line.rstrip()}  ->  {new.rstrip()}", file=sys.stderr)
            fout.write(new)
    print(f"{total} replacements on {lines_hit} lines -> {out_path}")
    return 0 if total else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```
範例：`./replace.py sim.log 'UVM_ERROR(\s+\S+\(\d+\))' 'UVM_WAIVED\1'`

### Explanation
- 用 `\b` 做完整單字比對，避免 `TIMEOUT` 誤換到 `TIMEOUT_CNT`。
- 用 capture group（Python 的 `\1`、sed 的 `\1`、Perl 的 `$1`）保留部分原文。
- 逐行處理 → 記憶體用量固定，幾 GB 的 log 也能處理。
- 寫到新檔或先備份，regression log 是證據，不要直接覆蓋。

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- 特殊字元：pattern 是一般字串而不是 regex 時，用 `re.escape()`；sed 裡的 `/` 可以換成 `s|a/b|c|g`。
- macOS 的 BSD `sed -i` 一定要給 suffix（`sed -i '' ...`）。
- 壓縮的 log：Python 用 `gzip.open(path, "rt")`；shell 用 `zcat f.gz | sed ... | gzip > out.gz`。
- 非 UTF-8 的位元組：用 `errors="replace"` 或以 binary 模式處理。

### Follow-ups
- *只在某段區間內取代？* sed：`sed '/START/,/END/s/foo/bar/g'`；Python 用狀態旗標。
- *多個檔案、遞迴目錄？* `grep -rl PATTERN dir | xargs perl -pi -e 's/PATTERN/NEW/g'`。

title: 偵測 `1101` 的 sequence detector FSM：畫出狀態機，在最後一個 `1` 時輸出拉高
solution:
**重點：** 「在最後一個 `1` 的同一拍輸出 1」就是 **Mealy** 機。state 代表「目前已經匹配的前綴長度」：`S0` = 空、`S1` = `1`、`S2` = `11`、`S3` = `110`。在 `S3` 收到 `1` 就輸出 1；overlapping 時回到 `S1`（因為 `1101` 的最長後綴＝前綴是 `1`）。

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> S0
  S0 --> S1: 1/0
  S0 --> S0: 0/0
  S1 --> S2: 1/0
  S1 --> S0: 0/0
  S2 --> S2: 1/0
  S2 --> S3: 0/0
  S3 --> S1: 1/1
  S3 --> S0: 0/0
```

### 推導重點
- `S2`（`11`）再收到 `1` → `111` 的後綴 `11` 仍然是前綴，所以留在 `S2`（不是回到 `S0`）。
- `S3`（`110`）收到 `0` → `1100` 沒有任何後綴是前綴 → `S0`。
- non-overlapping：`S3 --1/1--> S0`。

### Trace（輸入 `1101101`，overlapping）
| bit | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 0 | 1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| state 之前 | S0 | S1 | S2 | S3 | S1 | S2 | S3 |
| state 之後 | S1 | S2 | S3 | S1 | S2 | S3 | S1 |
| out | 0 | 0 | 0 | **1** | 0 | 0 | **1** |

第 4 個 bit 的 `1` 同時是第一個 `1101` 的結尾和第二個的開頭。

### Code
```systemverilog
module det1101 (input logic clk, rst_n, din, output logic dout);
  typedef enum logic [1:0] {S0, S1, S2, S3} state_t;
  state_t state, nxt;

  always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)
    if (!rst_n) state <= S0;
    else        state <= nxt;

  always_comb begin
    dout = 1'b0;
    unique case (state)
      S0: nxt = din ? S1 : S0;
      S1: nxt = din ? S2 : S0;
      S2: nxt = din ? S2 : S3;
      S3: begin
            nxt  = din ? S1 : S0;     // non-overlapping：nxt = S0
            dout = din;               // 最後一個 1 同一拍拉高
          end
      default: nxt = S0;
    endcase
  end
endmodule
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- 如果要求 registered output（Moore），就加一個 `S4` 輸出 1，輸出會晚一拍；`S4 --1--> S2`（`11011` 的後綴 `11`）、`S4 --0--> S0`。
- 常見錯誤：`S2` 收到 `1` 時回到 `S0` 或 `S1`，會漏掉 `11101`。
- reset 後立刻輸入 `1101`、連續 `1101101`、`111101` 都要測。

### Follow-ups
- *怎麼驗？* reference model 用 4-bit shift register：`dout_exp = ({sh[2:0], din} == 4'b1101)`，random 長串比對。
- *用 SVA 寫 checker？* `assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n) (din ##1 din ##1 !din ##1 din) |-> dout);`

title: Fibonacci：說明遞迴寫法
DUT 的 test plan：functional tests、不同頻率測試、reset tests、corner case 與 error case
solution:
**重點：** test plan 先從 spec 抽出 **feature list**，每個 feature 對應「怎麼打（stimulus）」、「怎麼檢查（checker）」、「怎麼證明打過（coverage）」。題目指定的五類：functional、不同頻率、reset、corner case、error case，各自列成章節，並定義完成標準（coverage 目標、regression pass rate）。

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  SPEC["spec / design doc"] --> FL["feature list"]
  FL --> F["functional tests"]
  FL --> CLK["clock frequency tests"]
  FL --> RST["reset tests"]
  FL --> CC["corner cases"]
  FL --> ERR["error cases"]
  F --> CHK["checkers: scoreboard + SVA"]
  CLK --> CHK
  RST --> CHK
  CC --> CHK
  ERR --> CHK
  CHK --> COV["coverage closure"]
  COV -->|holes| FL
```

### Test plan 範例（以「APB 設定介面 + 雙時脈資料路徑」的 DUT 為例）
| 類別 | 項目 | Stimulus | 檢查 / coverage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Functional | 每個 register 的 R/W、reset value | RAL built-in sequence | RAL mirror 比對 |
| Functional | 資料路徑各種模式、長度 | constrained random | scoreboard；mode × length cross |
| 頻率 | clk_a : clk_b 比例 1:1、1:4、4:1、非整數比 | 參數化 clock period、random phase | 資料不遺失；CDC SVA；ratio coverpoint |
| 頻率 | 最低 / 最高操作頻率、跑到一半改頻率 | 改 period plusarg | 吞吐量和 latency 符合規格 |
| Reset | power-on reset、傳輸中途 reset、兩個 domain 分別 reset | 在 random 時間點 assert reset | reset 後所有 output / flag 回到預設值；scoreboard flush |
| Reset | async assert / sync deassert | reset 在 clock edge 附近 deassert | 不出現 X；reset synchronizer 的 SVA |
| Corner | FIFO 剛好 full / empty、計數器 wrap、最大 / 最小長度 | directed + 偏重邊界的 constraint | 邊界值 bins |
| Corner | back-to-back、長時間 idle、同時事件 | 0 間隔與長間隔的分布 | 時序 cover property |
| Error | 非法位址、非法設定、protocol violation、parity / CRC error | error-injection callback | 錯誤 status / interrupt 有被設定，而且 DUT 能復原 |

### Code：可設定頻率的 clock 和傳輸中途的 reset
```systemverilog
module tb;
  timeunit 1ps; timeprecision 1ps;
  int unsigned clka_ps = 10_000, clkb_ps = 3_333;   // 100 MHz / ~300 MHz
  logic clk_a = 0, clk_b = 0, rst_n = 0;

  initial begin
    void'($value$plusargs("CLKA_PS=%d", clka_ps));   // regression 掃描不同頻率
    void'($value$plusargs("CLKB_PS=%d", clkb_ps));
    #($urandom_range(clkb_ps));                      // random 起始相位
    forever #(clkb_ps / 2) clk_b = ~clk_b;
  end
  always #(clka_ps / 2) clk_a = ~clk_a;

  // 傳輸中途在 random 時間點 reset
  task automatic mid_traffic_reset();
    repeat ($urandom_range(50, 500)) @(posedge clk_a);
    #($urandom_range(clka_ps - 1)) rst_n = 0;        // 不對齊 edge 的非同步 assert
    repeat (5) @(posedge clk_a);
    @(negedge clk_a) rst_n = 1;
  endtask
endmodule
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- 只測 1:1 頻率會漏掉 CDC 問題；一定要有快 → 慢、慢 → 快。
- 中途 reset 後，TB 本身（scoreboard 的 queue、driver 狀態、objection）也要正確 reset，否則會出現假 fail。
- error case 要驗證 **復原**：錯誤之後再送正常傳輸，必須正確。
- 每個項目都要有對應的 coverage，否則無法證明「測過」。

### Follow-ups
- *怎麼排優先順序？* 依風險：新功能、複雜 FSM、CDC 和 reset 最優先，再來是低機率 corner case。
- *怎麼知道 test plan 完成？* functional coverage 100%（或有 waiver）、code coverage 的漏洞都有審查、所有 test 在多個 seed 下穩定 pass。

title: 反轉 linked list
陣列中最長的 peak
Parity flag 電路
answer: encoder 輸出 2-bit code（X、Y、W、Z）。當 X 出現偶數次 **且** W 出現奇數次時，`Flag = 1`。用最少的 gate（AND / OR / XOR / MUX）畫出電路。
solution:
**重點：** 只在乎次數的**奇偶**，所以每個符號只需要一個 1-bit 的 toggle flop（T flip-flop = 自己 XOR 偵測訊號），不需要計數器。為了省掉輸出端的 inverter，X 的 flop 存 **x_even**（reset 成 1，因為 0 次是偶數），W 的 flop 存 **w_odd**（reset 成 0）。`Flag = x_even AND w_odd`。

### 編碼假設（題目原文模糊，先和面試官確認）
| code[1:0] | 符號 | x_even 的 toggle | w_odd 的 toggle |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 00 | X | 1 | 0 |
| 01 | Y | 0 | 0 |
| 10 | W | 0 | 1 |
| 11 | Z | 0 | 0 |

### 電路
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C["code c1 c0, valid"] --> DX["isX = valid AND NOT c1 AND NOT c0"]
  C --> DW["isW = valid AND c1 AND NOT c0"]
  DX --> XX["XOR"]
  XE["DFF x_even, reset 1"] --> XX
  XX --> XE
  DW --> XW["XOR"]
  WO["DFF w_odd, reset 0"] --> XW
  XW --> WO
  XE --> AND["AND"]
  WO --> AND
  AND --> F["Flag"]
```
gate 數：decode 共用 `valid AND NOT c0` → 2 個 AND 分出 isX / isW（再加 c1 的反相），2 個 XOR，1 個 AND 輸出，2 個 DFF。

```wavedrom
{ "signal": [
  { "name": "clk",    "wave": "p......." },
  { "name": "code",   "wave": "x=====x.", "data": ["W","X","W","X","W"] },
  { "name": "x_even", "wave": "1..0.1.." },
  { "name": "w_odd",  "wave": "0.1.0.1." },
  { "name": "Flag",   "wave": "0.10..1." }
],
  "head": { "text": "Flag = 1 when #X is even and #W is odd (registered counts)" } }
```

### Code
```systemverilog
module parity_flag (
  input  logic       clk, rst_n, valid,
  input  logic [1:0] code,          // 00=X 01=Y 10=W 11=Z
  output logic       flag
);
  logic x_even, w_odd;
  wire  is_x = valid && (code == 2'b00);
  wire  is_w = valid && (code == 2'b10);

  always_ff @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n)
    if (!rst_n) begin
      x_even <= 1'b1;               // 0 個 X = 偶數
      w_odd  <= 1'b0;               // 0 個 W = 偶數
    end else begin
      x_even <= x_even ^ is_x;      // T flip-flop
      w_odd  <= w_odd  ^ is_w;
    end

  assign flag = x_even & w_odd;
endmodule
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- reset 後還沒有任何輸入：X = 0 次（偶數）、W = 0 次（偶數）→ Flag = 0。
- 如果 Flag 要**包含這一拍的輸入**（組合輸出），就改成 `(x_even ^ is_x) & (w_odd ^ is_w)`，代價是 input → output 的組合路徑。
- 沒有 `valid` 的話，idle 的時候 code 不能停在 `00` 或 `10`，否則會一直 toggle。
- 只用 MUX 也可以做 toggle：`x_even_n = is_x ? ~x_even : x_even`。

### Follow-ups
- *如果條件改成「X 出現 3 的倍數次」？* 需要 mod-3 計數器（2 個 flop），不能再用單一 XOR。
- *怎麼驗？* reference model 直接計數 `nx`、`nw`，比較 `flag == (nx % 2 == 0 && nw % 2 == 1)`；coverage 收四種奇偶組合。

title: In a large verification environment, how would you efficiently propagate configurations from a `uvm_test` class to various components inside a `uvm_env`?
Your testbench has synchronization issues where transactions sent by the `uvm_sequencer` reach the `uvm_driver` too late. How would you debug and fix this using UVM phases?
You need a component to execute additional tasks after `run_phase` but before `check_phase`. Which UVM phase would you use, and how?
A `uvm_sequence` must generate a burst of transactions with a burst size controlled dynamically at runtime. How would you implement this?
How would you handle arbitration between multiple sequences running on the same `uvm_sequencer`?
solution:
**Key idea:** When several sequences call `start_item()` on one sequencer, the sequencer's **arbitration mode** (`set_arbitration`) and each sequence's **priority** (third argument of `start()`) decide who gets the driver next. For exclusive access use **`lock()`** (waits its turn) or **`grab()`** (jumps the queue); to make a sequence skip arbitration temporarily, override **`is_relevant()`**. For custom policies use `UVM_SEQ_ARB_USER` and override `user_priority_arbitration()`.

| Mode | Behavior | Priority used? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `UVM_SEQ_ARB_FIFO` (default) | grant in request order | no |
| `UVM_SEQ_ARB_WEIGHTED` | random, weighted by priority | as weight |
| `UVM_SEQ_ARB_RANDOM` | uniform random | no |
| `UVM_SEQ_ARB_STRICT_FIFO` | highest priority first; FIFO among equals | yes |
| `UVM_SEQ_ARB_STRICT_RANDOM` | highest priority first; random among equals | yes |
| `UVM_SEQ_ARB_USER` | `user_priority_arbitration()` decides | your choice |

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant T1 as traffic_seq A
  participant T2 as traffic_seq B
  participant IRQ as irq_seq (priority 500)
  participant SQR as sequencer (STRICT_FIFO)
  participant DRV as driver
  T1->>SQR: request
  T2->>SQR: request
  IRQ->>SQR: request
  SQR-->>IRQ: grant (highest priority)
  IRQ->>DRV: item
  SQR-->>T1: grant (FIFO among priority 100)
  T1->>DRV: item
  SQR-->>T2: grant
```

### Code
```systemverilog
class arb_test extends base_test;
  `uvm_component_utils(arb_test)
  function new(string name, uvm_component parent); super.new(name, parent); endfunction

  task main_phase(uvm_phase phase);
    traffic_seq a   = traffic_seq::type_id::create("a");
    traffic_seq b   = traffic_seq::type_id::create("b");
    irq_seq     irq = irq_seq::type_id::create("irq");
    phase.raise_objection(this);
    env.agt.sqr.set_arbitration(UVM_SEQ_ARB_STRICT_FIFO);
    fork
      a.start(env.agt.sqr, null, 100);
      b.start(env.agt.sqr, null, 100);
      begin #500ns; irq.start(env.agt.sqr, null, 500); end   // pre-empts at item boundaries
    join
    phase.drop_objection(this);
  endtask
endclass

// Atomic multi-item operation: no other sequence can interleave
class cfg_burst_seq extends uvm_sequence #(bus_item);
  `uvm_object_utils(cfg_burst_seq)
  function new(string name = "cfg_burst_seq"); super.new(name); endfunction
  task body();
    lock(m_sequencer);              // grab(m_sequencer) would jump ahead of waiting requests
    repeat (4) `uvm_do(req)
    unlock(m_sequencer);
  endtask
endclass

// Custom policy: always pick the most recent requester (LIFO)
class lifo_sequencer extends uvm_sequencer #(bus_item);
  `uvm_component_utils(lifo_sequencer)
  function new(string name, uvm_component parent); super.new(name, parent); endfunction
  function integer user_priority_arbitration(integer avail_sequences[$]);
    return avail_sequences[avail_sequences.size() - 1];   // must return an entry of the list
  endfunction
endclass
```

### Explanation
- Arbitration happens **per item**, at each `start_item()`/`wait_for_grant()`; a higher-priority sequence cannot interrupt an item already handed to the driver.
- Default priority is 100 (passing `-1`); priorities only matter in `WEIGHTED`, `STRICT_*` or `USER` modes.
- `is_relevant()` returning 0 removes a sequence from arbitration (for example, a background sequence that idles while a flag is set); implement `wait_for_relevant()` too.

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- Starvation: `STRICT_*` with a high-priority sequence that never stops blocks everyone else.
- Forgetting `unlock()` (or the locking sequence being killed) leaves the sequencer locked; `kill()` releases locks, but stopping threads with `disable fork` may not.
- Two sequences that both `lock` and wait on each other's results can deadlock.
- In a layered environment, priorities are per sequencer; set them on the sequencer where the contention happens.

### Follow-ups
- *`lock` vs `grab`?* Both give exclusive access; `lock` waits in the arbitration queue, `grab` goes to the front (still after a current lock).
- *How to verify fairness?* Record grants per sequence in a coverage model or count them in the test and check the ratio.

title: Explain the UVM factory mechanism. How does `set_type_override` differ from `set_inst_override`?
solution:
**Key idea:** The factory is a central registry: `` `uvm_component_utils``/`` `uvm_object_utils`` register a class (a proxy `type_id`), and `type_id::create()` asks the factory "what type should I actually build here?". Overrides change the answer without editing the code that creates the object. **`set_type_override`** replaces the type **everywhere**; **`set_inst_override`** replaces it only for objects whose **hierarchical path matches**, and instance overrides take **precedence** over type overrides.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  C["bus_driver::type_id::create('drv', this)"] --> I{"instance override matches full path?"}
  I -->|yes| IO["build instance-override type"]
  I -->|no| T{"type override for bus_driver?"}
  T -->|yes| TO["build type-override type"]
  T -->|no| O["build bus_driver"]
```

| | `set_type_override` | `set_inst_override` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scope | every `create()` of the original type | only objects whose path matches (wildcards allowed) |
| Arguments | original type, override type, `replace` flag | relative/full path, original type, override type |
| Precedence | lower | higher, checked first |
| Typical use | swap the item or driver for a whole test (error injection) | one agent out of many behaves differently |
| Command line | `+uvm_set_type_override=bus_driver,err_driver` | `+uvm_set_inst_override=bus_driver,slow_driver,uvm_test_top.env.agt0.drv` |

### Code
```systemverilog
class err_driver  extends bus_driver;
  `uvm_component_utils(err_driver)
  function new(string name, uvm_component parent); super.new(name, parent); endfunction
endclass
class slow_driver extends bus_driver;
  `uvm_component_utils(slow_driver)
  function new(string name, uvm_component parent); super.new(name, parent); endfunction
endclass

class override_test extends base_test;
  `uvm_component_utils(override_test)
  function new(string name, uvm_component parent); super.new(name, parent); endfunction

  function void build_phase(uvm_phase phase);
    // every bus_driver becomes err_driver ...
    set_type_override_by_type(bus_driver::get_type(), err_driver::get_type());
    // ... except env.agt0.drv (path relative to this test), which becomes slow_driver
    set_inst_override_by_type("env.agt0.drv", bus_driver::get_type(), slow_driver::get_type());
    // equivalent static forms:
    //   bus_driver::type_id::set_type_override(err_driver::get_type());
    //   bus_driver::type_id::set_inst_override(slow_driver::get_type(), "env.agt0.drv", this);
    super.build_phase(phase);     // overrides must exist before env builds the agents
  endfunction

  function void end_of_elaboration_phase(uvm_phase phase);
    uvm_factory factory = uvm_factory::get();
    factory.print();              // lists registered types and active overrides
    uvm_top.print_topology();     // agt0.drv: slow_driver, agt1.drv: err_driver
  endfunction
endclass
```

### Explanation
- `create()` passes the parent's full name plus the instance name to the factory, which first searches instance overrides by path, then type overrides; overrides chain (if `err_driver` is itself overridden, the chain is followed).
- The override type must be a **subclass** of the original, or the `$cast` inside `create()` fails.
- For objects (sequence items), instance overrides match against the context path: items created inside a sequence use the sequencer path plus sequence name, so wildcard paths such as `"*.agt0.sqr.*"` are common.

### Corner cases & pitfalls
- Objects built with `new()` bypass the factory entirely.
- Overrides set after the component was created have no effect on it.
- By-name overrides (`set_type_override("bus_driver", "err_driver")`) need string registration, which parameterized classes lack.
- With `replace = 0`, an existing type override is kept instead of replaced.

### Follow-ups
- *How do you check which override won?* `factory.debug_create_by_type(bus_driver::get_type(), "uvm_test_top.env.agt0", "drv")` prints the decision.
- *Overriding a sequence?* Same mechanism: `base_seq::type_id::set_type_override(err_seq::get_type())`, provided the sequence is created with `type_id::create`.

title: How do you integrate functional coverage with UVM? What are the differences between `uvm_subscriber` and `uvm_analysis_port`?
solution:
> Generated by Gemini via agy. **Key idea:** Functional coverage is integrated by wrapping covergroups inside dedicated subscriber components connected to monitor analysis ports, where `uvm_analysis_port` is the broadcasting publisher and `uvm_subscriber` is the receiving consumer implementing `write()`. ```mermaid flowchart LR MON["uvm_monitor
(Producer)"] -->|write| SUB_NODE["uvm_subscriber
(Consumer / Coverage)"] MON -->|write| SCB["uvm_scoreboard
(Consumer / Checker)"] subgraph SUB_BOX ["Coverage Subscriber Component"] IMP["uvm_analysis_imp analysis_export"] --> W["function void write(T t)"] W --> CG["covergroup.sample()"] end ``` ### Explanation - **Functional Coverage Integration:** - Avoid sampling functional coverage directly inside the monitor; keep the monitor focused solely on pin extraction. - Create a dedicated coverage collector component derived from `uvm_subscriber #(trans_item)`. - Inside the subscriber, declare and instantiate a `covergroup`. - In `env::connect_phase()`, connect the monitor's analysis port to the subscriber's analysis export: `agent.monitor.ap.connect(cov_subscriber.analysis_export);` - In the subscriber's `write(trans_item t)` implementation, assign `t` to a local variable and invoke `covergroup.sample()`. - **`uvm_analysis_port` vs `uvm_subscriber`:** | Feature | `uvm_analysis_port #(T)` | `uvm_subscriber #(T)` | |---|---|---| | Role | **Producer / Broadcaster** (Outgoing TLM port) | **Consumer** (Complete testbench component) | | Component vs Port | TLM Port object instantiated inside a component | Full `uvm_component` with hierarchy and phases | | Internal Interface | Contains broadcast method: `write(T t)` | Encapsulates `uvm_analysis_imp` and defines pure virtual `write(T t)` | | Typical Location | Instantiated inside `uvm_monitor` or `uvm_agent` | Standalone component inside `uvm_env` | ### Corner cases & pitfalls - **Blocking in Subscriber `write()`:** Because `write()` is a SystemVerilog function, it cannot contain blocking delays (`#`, `@`); attempting to synchronize with clocks inside `write()` will fail to compile. - **Reference Contamination:** If the monitor reuses the same transaction object across cycles without cloning, the subscriber's sampled data may be corrupted by subsequent transactions. ### Follow-ups - Can multiple subscribers connect to one analysis port? Yes, `uvm_analysis_port` implements an observer pattern that broadcasts to any number of connected subscribers. - How to sample coverage conditioned on DUT state? Pass sideband control flags in the sequence item or evaluate conditional expressions inside coverpoint `iff (enable)`.

title: You are verifying AXI transactions that may complete out of order. How would you design the scoreboard to match transactions correctly?
A `uvm_sequence` generates random stimulus, but conflicting constraints cause randomization failures. How would you debug and resolve the constraint issues?
solution:
> Generated by Gemini via agy. **Key idea:** Debugging constraint conflicts involves enabling simulator solver debug flags to identify the Minimal Unsatisfiable Core (MUC), selectively isolating constraint blocks with `constraint_mode(0)`, and resolving conflicts by rewriting bounds or using `soft` constraints. ```mermaid flowchart TD FAIL["Randomization Failure (randomize() returns 0)"] --> STEP1["Enable Simulator Solver Diagnostics
- VCS: +ntb_solver_debug=verbose
- Questa: set SolveFailDebug=1
- Xcelium: -simsolverprofile"] STEP1 --> MUC["Analyze Minimal Unsatisfiable Core (MUC)
Simulator logs exact conflicting equations"] MUC --> LOCATE{"Where does the conflict originate?"} LOCATE -->|Inline with constraint conflict| FIX1["Resolve inline with { } constraint against class constraint"] LOCATE -->|Default vs Specific mode conflict| FIX2["Declare base constraint as 'soft' to permit override"] LOCATE -->|State variable dependency| FIX3["Verify pre_randomize() values are not over-constraining"] LOCATE -->|Complex interdependent blocks| STEP2["Isolate with item.constraint_mode(0)
Re-enable blocks one by one to find collision"] ``` ### Explanation - **Step 1: Leverage Solver Diagnostic Tools:** - Modern simulators provide solver diagnostic flags that isolate the exact set of contradictory constraints (Minimal Unsatisfiable Core): - *Synopsys VCS:* `+ntb_solver_debug=verbose` and `+ntb_stop_on_solver_error=1`. - *Siemens Questa:* `set SolveFailDebug 1` and run with `-solvefaildebug`. - *Cadence Xcelium:* `-sv_spec_fail` or `+xm_solver_debug`. - **Step 2: Check for Inline Constraint Contradictions:** - A common cause is a sequence calling `req.randomize() with { addr == 32'h0; }` when the item's class definition has `constraint c_addr { addr > 32'h100; }`. - **Step 3: Systematic Isolation with `constraint_mode`:** - Turn off all constraints on the object: `item.constraint_mode(0);`. - Re-enable constraint blocks one by one (`item.c_addr.constraint_mode(1);`) until randomization fails, pinpointing the colliding block. - **Step 4: Use `soft` Constraints:** - Mark default class constraints with the `soft` keyword: `constraint c_default_len { soft length inside {[1:10]}; }` - Inline constraints in sequences will override soft constraints without causing solver failures. ### Corner cases & pitfalls - **Cyclic Dependencies:** Inadvertently creating circular relationships (e.g., $A > B, B > C, C > A$) creates unsolvable constraint matrices. - **Unchecked Randomization:** Always wrap `randomize()` inside an assertion: `if (!item.randomize()) `uvm_fatal(...)`. Never execute unconstrained or failed items. ### Follow-ups - How to check if a specific constraint is active? Call `item.c_name.constraint_mode()`. - What is `rand_mode(0)`? It disables randomization for a specific variable, turning it into a fixed state variable during solver evaluation.

title: Your testbench has multiple interfaces, such as AXI and SPI. How would you use a virtual sequence to coordinate stimulus across both interfaces?
Write an assertion check to make sure that a signal is high for a minimum of 2 cycles and a maximum of 6 cycles
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** Count the rising sample as the first high cycle, require two through six consecutive highs, then require a low.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| High at t0,t1; low at t2 | Pass: length 2 |
| High t0..t5; low t6 | Pass: length 6 |
| High t0 only, or high through t6 | Fail |

### Explanation
The terminating low is essential: high[*2:6] alone can match the first two cycles of an indefinitely high signal. This property starts an attempt at each sampled rise. Reset interrupts the pulse-length requirement; if the signal starts high after reset, decide whether that should count as a new observed pulse. All properties use rising-edge sampling on clk. Unless stated otherwise, rst_n is an active-low reset and disable iff (!rst_n) aborts pending attempts during reset. Controls are assumed known 0/1; add explicit unknown checks when X/Z must be reported.

### Code
```systemverilog
assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
  $rose(signal_a) |-> signal_a[*2:6] ##1 !signal_a);
cover property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
  $rose(signal_a) ##1 signal_a ##1 !signal_a);
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
A clocked checker measures sampled pulse length, not physical pulse width. A pulse wholly between edges is invisible. End-of-test before the allowed pulse ends must be handled by the test's drain policy or a strong consequent if pending obligations must fail.

### Follow-ups
To require exactly four high samples, replace [*2:6] with [*4] and retain the final !signal_a.

title: Write an assertion checker to make sure that an output signal never goes X?
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** Assert that no bit of the output is X or Z at every valid sampling event.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| out = 8'h00 | Pass |
| out = 8'b10x00000 | Fail |
| out = 8'b0000000z | Fail |

### Explanation
$isunknown checks the entire packed expression. Logical comparisons to X are unsuitable because ordinary equality with unknown operands produces X. Declare the observed net as four-state logic: converting it to bit before checking destroys the evidence. The reset exemption should match whether output is specified during reset. All properties use rising-edge sampling on clk. Unless stated otherwise, rst_n is an active-low reset and disable iff (!rst_n) aborts pending attempts during reset. Controls are assumed known 0/1; add explicit unknown checks when X/Z must be reported.

### Code
```systemverilog
assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
  !$isunknown(out));
// Optional validity qualifier when output is meaningful only on valid:
assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
  valid |-> !$isunknown(out));
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
These are alternative contracts: the first checks every active sample, while the second permits unknown output when valid is low. Neither proves absence of between-edge glitches. If “never” is literal continuous simulation behavior, add an event-driven immediate check with a clearly specified startup/settling policy.

### Follow-ups
How do you check several signals? Apply !$isunknown({valid, ready, data}) to their concatenation, with validity qualification appropriate to data.

title: Write an assertion to make sure that a 5-bit grant signal only has one bit set at any time?
Write an assertion which checks that once a valid request is asserted by the master, the arbiter provides a grant within 2 to 5 clock cycles
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** A request sampled at t0 requires grant on at least one sample t2 through t5.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| t0 | Request rises |
| t1 | Too early to satisfy this obligation |
| t2,t3,t4,t5 | Any grant satisfies the window |
| No grant by t5 | Fail |

### Explanation
This version treats a rising valid_request as a new request. For one-cycle request pulses, valid_request can be used directly. The overlapped implication starts at t0, so the explicit delay range is exactly two through five cycles. The property requires a grant in the window; it does not by itself forbid earlier grants or associate grants with unique requests. All properties use rising-edge sampling on clk. Unless stated otherwise, rst_n is an active-low reset and disable iff (!rst_n) aborts pending attempts during reset. Controls are assumed known 0/1; add explicit unknown checks when X/Z must be reported.

### Code
```systemverilog
assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
  $rose(valid_request) |-> ##[2:5] grant);
cover property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
  $rose(valid_request) ##5 grant);
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
Multiple requests may have overlapping response windows and one grant can satisfy several attempts. Use an outstanding-request model if each request must consume a separate grant. A level trigger starts a new attempt every high cycle, which is wrong if the requester holds its request pending service.

### Follow-ups
For exactly three cycles, use ##3. For “not before two cycles,” also forbid grant in the early interval under the chosen request-ownership model.

title: How can you disable an assertion during active reset time?
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** disable iff aborts active assertion attempts while reset is asserted and prevents new checks until reset is inactive.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Request starts, then reset asserts | Attempt aborted |
| Reset remains low | No new checking |
| Reset released | New attempts may start |

### Explanation
For active-low reset, the disabling Boolean is !rst_n. This is an asynchronous abort condition, not an antecedent saying that reset was inactive when the sequence began. Gating only the antecedent leaves an already active consequent alive through reset, which often produces misleading failures. Decide whether reset is intended to cancel transactions or whether some requirements must survive it. All properties use rising-edge sampling on clk. Unless stated otherwise, rst_n is an active-low reset and disable iff (!rst_n) aborts pending attempts during reset. Controls are assumed known 0/1; add explicit unknown checks when X/Z must be reported.

### Code
```systemverilog
assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
  req |=> ack);
// If unknown reset must also disable checking:
// assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (rst_n !== 1'b1)
//   req |=> ack);
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
disable iff uses current, unsampled reset semantics, which can matter when reset changes in the same slot as the clock. A reset checker itself must not be disabled by the reset condition it is supposed to examine. An X reset needs an explicit policy: mask it, fail it, or both in separate checks.

### Follow-ups
For synchronous reset cancellation, use a sampled condition or appropriate synchronous-abort operator and document the exact clock semantics instead of assuming disable iff is synchronous.

title: As long as signal_a is up, signal_b should not be asserted. Write an assertion
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** Disallow signal_b on every sample where signal_a is high.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| a=1,b=0 | Pass |
| a=1,b=1 | Fail on this sample |
| a=0,b=1 | Allowed |

### Explanation
This is a same-sample mutual-exclusion rule rather than a delayed response. An overlapped implication checks b at the sample that triggered a. Equivalently, assert !(signal_a && signal_b) every clock. The expression does not constrain b when a is low, and it makes no claim about the future value of either signal. All properties use rising-edge sampling on clk. Unless stated otherwise, rst_n is an active-low reset and disable iff (!rst_n) aborts pending attempts during reset. Controls are assumed known 0/1; add explicit unknown checks when X/Z must be reported.

### Code
```systemverilog
assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
  signal_a |-> !signal_b);
assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
  !$isunknown({signal_a, signal_b}));
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
Using |=> accidentally allows a and b together now and prohibits b only next cycle. If a never asserts, the implication passes vacuously; cover a while b is low to show the relevant scenario occurred. These sampled checks do not detect a brief overlap between clock edges.

title: The signal_a is a pulse; it can only be asserted for one cycle, and must be deasserted in the next cycle

title: Signal_a and signal_b can only be asserted together for one cycle; in the next cycle, at least one of them must be deasserted
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

title: When signal_a is asserted, signal_b must be asserted, and must remain up until one of the signals signal_c or signal_d is asserted

title: signal_a must not be asserted together with signal_b or with signal_c
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |

| a,b,c = 1,1,0 or 1,0,1 | Illegal |
| a,b,c = 0,1,1 | Legal |

title: In a RESP operation, request must be true immediately, grant must be true 3 clock cycles later, followed by request being false, and then grant being false
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** On a RESP trigger, require req now, grant at +3, req low at +4, and grant low at +5.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |

| t0: RESP event | req=1 |
| t3 | grant=1 |
| t4 | req=0 |
| t5 | grant=0 |

title: Request must true at the current cycle; grant must become true sometime between 1 cycle after request and the end of time
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** A request at the current sample requires a later grant, with no finite latency bound.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| req at t0 | Trigger |
| grant at t0 only | Does not satisfy later grant |
| grant at any t>=1 | Satisfies eventuality |
| No later grant | Liveness violation |

### Explanation


title: Req must eventually be followed by ack, which must be followed 1 cycle later by done
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** After req, require a later ack and done exactly one cycle after that ack.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| req at t0 | Start obligation |
| ack at tK, K>=1 | Response |
| done at tK+1 | Required |

title: The active-low reset must be low for at least 6 clock cycles
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** On reset assertion, count the first sampled low as cycle one and require six consecutive low samples.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| t0: reset falls | Low sample 1 |
| t1..t5 | Low samples 2..6 |
| t6 | May rise, but need not |

### Explanation
The reset-duration assertion must remain enabled during reset, so it deliberately has no disable iff on rst_n. The repetition includes the triggering sample because |-> is overlapped. It enforces a minimum duration and allows reset to remain low indefinitely. This is a sampled-cycle requirement, not a continuous elapsed-time guarantee. All properties use rising-edge sampling on clk. Unless stated otherwise, rst_n is an active-low reset and disable iff (!rst_n) aborts pending attempts during reset.   $fell(rst_n) |-> !rst_n[*6]);

```systemverilog
  $fell(rst_n) ##5 !rst_n ##1 rst_n);
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls

Define and test startup reset explicitly; an initialization controller or separate startup check may be needed. If the clock is stopped during reset, six sampled clocks cannot be counted. title: Enable must remain true throughout the entire ack to done sequence
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** Require enable from the ack sample through the done sample, including both endpoints.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| t0: ack rises | enable=1 |
| t1..tK-1 | enable stays 1 |
| tK: done | enable still 1 |

If completion is mandatory, the strong variant s_until_with adds that requirement. If done is already high when ack rises, the interval ends immediately and enable is still required on that sample. ```systemverilog

```systemverilog
  $rose(ack) |-> (enable until_with done));
// If eventual completion is also required:
// $rose(ack) |-> (enable s_until_with done)
```

title: Write an assertion for glitch detection
If signal_a is active, then signal_b was active 3 cycles ago
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** Guard the history depth, then require b at the sample exactly three cycles before every active a.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| t0: b=1 | Historical event |
| t1,t2 | Intermediate samples |
| t3: a=1 | Pass using b at t0 |

### Explanation
$past(signal_b,3) means three sampling events, not three time units. A saturating history counter prevents the first three post-reset samples from referring to pre-reset or unavailable history. This example exempts early a samples; if early a itself is illegal, add a check that a implies history==3 instead of silently exempting them. All properties use rising-edge sampling on clk. Unless stated otherwise, rst_n is an active-low reset and disable iff (!rst_n) aborts pending attempts during reset. Controls are assumed known 0/1; add explicit unknown checks when X/Z must be reported.

### Code
```systemverilog
int unsigned history = 0;
always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
  if (!rst_n) history <= 0;
  else if (history < 3) history <= history + 1;
end
assert property (@(posedge clk) disable iff (!rst_n)
  history == 3 && signal_a |-> $past(signal_b, 3));
```

### Corner cases & pitfalls
Do not shift the implication into the future: the requirement is about the past relative to current a. A b that is high now cannot repair a missing b three cycles ago. The counter and assertion both use sampled pre-NBA values, giving three completed historical edges before checking begins.

### Follow-ups
If b must have risen three cycles ago rather than simply been high, check a guarded $past($rose(signal_b),3) and provide enough startup history for the edge detector too.

title: If the state machine reaches active1 state, it will eventually reach active2 state
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** Reaching active1 starts a liveness obligation to reach active2 at some later sample.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| t0: state=ACTIVE1 | Obligation starts |
| t1..tK-1 | Other states may occur |
| tK: state=ACTIVE2 | Obligation satisfied |

The title does not state a deadline, so the property uses an unbounded future search beginning one cycle after active1. strong requires an actual match rather than allowing an unfinished sequence at simulation termination. A level state comparison creates an obligation on every active1 sample; use an entry detector if only entering the state should start one. All properties use rising-edge sampling on clk. Unless stated otherwise, rst_n is an active-low reset and disable iff (!rst_n) aborts pending attempts during reset.   state == ACTIVE1 |-> strong(##[1:$] (state == ACTIVE2)));


title: Write an assertion: A high for 5 cycles and B high after 4 continuous highs of A and finally both A and B are high?
solution:
> Completed by Codex.

**Key idea:** One clear interpretation is A high for exactly five sampled cycles, B first high on the fifth, with both high on that final cycle.

| Sample / case | Expected behavior |
| --- | --- |
| t0..t3 | A=1, B=0: four continuous highs |
| t4 | A=1, B=1: fifth high and overlap |
| t5 | A=0: ends exact five-cycle run |

The wording is ambiguous about whether B may be high earlier and whether A must drop after five cycles. This answer states the stricter exact-length interpretation explicitly. An A rise starts the run, overlapped implication counts that sample as the first A high, and [*4] covers t0..t3. The next sample is the required A/B overlap. All properties use rising-edge sampling on clk. Unless stated otherwise, rst_n is an active-low reset and disable iff (!rst_n) aborts pending attempts during reset.   $rose(A) |-> (A && !B)[*4] ##1 (A && B) ##1 !A);

If A only needs to be high for at least five cycles, remove the trailing ##1 !A. If B may already be high during the first four samples, replace (A && !B)[*4] with A[*4]. These changes broaden the legal traces and must be chosen from the intended specification, not from convenience.
